description: Cursor-Governance binding to the canonical memory control plane (l9-graphiti-memory). Read by ops/memory/runtime_binding.py, which proves the exact package, interpreter, and console script before any lifecycle call. This is a Cursor-owned statement of what Cursor expects to run; it grants nothing and resolves no provider. Production binding is an immutable release artifact locked in uv.lock; MEMORY_TARGET_VERSION is release 2.3.0 (cut at campaign stage M2 on the memory PR); integration binds the exact git SHA of that release below until the v2.3.0 tag is on origin and uv.lock carries the artifact.

source.ref_note: Release 2.3.0 = MEMORY_TARGET_VERSION, and this is the commit tag v2.3.0 resolves to (annotated tag 03ec559ca8e28b49c6763189363fc55400e3b09d, peeled target 5605569b). The tag is the release identity, so source.ref must equal its target: a release_tag the manifest cannot resolve to its own ref is a claim, not a binding. 5605569b is an ancestor of origin/main, merged by 7691c07648d319ad22b353f4f6cb7e164f746bb2, and the two carry the identical tree d38f10d7e7800a80d3c5cdff3affdf93220cf981 — so the wheel, artifact_sha256, and every proof taken against them are unchanged by which of the two is named. uv.lock still cannot pin the artifact: the package is not on PyPI (404 for both l9-graphite-memory and l9-graphiti-memory as of 2026-09-07) and this surface cannot read the releases API to confirm a release asset. Lock it once an index or asset serves it — that is what uv sync --locked --no-build needs.

binding_policy.production: exact release artifact locked in uv.lock; runtime_mode=pinned_environment
binding_policy.integration: exact git SHA above, installed as a built wheel into the governance environment; runtime_mode=pinned_environment
binding_policy.development: L9_MEMORY_DEV_CHECKOUT=<path to a l9-graphiti-memory checkout with .venv>; runtime_mode=development_checkout, never silent
forbidden: whatever l9-memory is first on PATH
an adjacent checkout discovered by directory scanning
pip install -e of a sibling checkout without the development opt-in

release_evidence.description: Exact-head proof of the binding (audit P1-01/P2-02). The wheel is built from source.ref with uv build --wheel under the fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH below and is byte-reproducible (the digest reproduced from a fresh clone of the same commit). .github/workflows/memory-cross-repo.yml rebuilds it from the same ref, refuses a digest mismatch, installs the wheel into a clean environment, and runs tests/ops/memory/test_cross_repo_lifecycle.py with L9_MEMORY_CROSS_REPO_REQUIRED=1 (a skip is a failure) and no provider credential in the environment. A digest here without that job green on the same Cursor head is a claim, not a proof.
operator_gated: uv.lock pin of the released artifact (replaces the git SHA source)
release_evidence.artifact_provenance_note: In-place artifact proof needs a PEP 610 archive hash, which pip/uv record for index and URL installs but NOT for the local-file install the proof workflow performs. So the workflow proves the artifact instead, and more strongly: it rebuilds the wheel from source.ref and refuses any sha256 other than artifact_sha256 before installing. The binding reports 'compatible' there and says why. L9_MEMORY_REQUIRE_EXACT_ARTIFACT=1 remains for environments whose installer records provenance.
release_evidence.installed_record_digest_note: RETRACTED as an exactness proof, on evidence. FOUR installs of the byte-identical wheel (artifact_sha256 re-verified by rebuild each time) produced four different installed-RECORD digests: fbe247ae..., 7c875776..., be59801c... on GitHub runners and 52b6df58... in a Claude Code container — the last three under identical normalisation. The installed RECORD is therefore not a deterministic function of the wheel, and a pin would flap the binding between exact and unbound on an unchanged release. runtime_binding still verifies a RECORD digest when one is pinned; nothing pins one until it is shown stable across machines.
release_evidence.memory_sha_note: The commit tag v2.3.0 peels to. This binding moved twice on 2026-09-07 and both moves are recorded rather than rewritten: #56's PR head 5605569b -> its merge commit 7691c076 when the PR merged and no tag existed (a pre-final branch head is not a release identity), then back to 5605569b when the release authority cut v2.3.0 there. The tag settles it: the tagged commit IS the release, and it is an ancestor of main. Nothing about the artifact moved with either rebind — one tree d38f10d7, one wheel, digest 905d91402db99fcd3e094db67576c19297823b448fd6f76842f32d1be4804291 reproduced from both.

contract_model_aliases._note: Cursor view name -> the model names the bound release actually exports, discovered from the schema probe's `available` list in the memory-cross-repo job. Cursor requests its own name; the probe accepts any alias, and the schema is keyed by the Cursor name so validation lookup is unchanged. A name this side guessed is not a contract the release owes.
contract_model_aliases._verified: All five aliases plus PhaseLockVerification and GroupResolution were read from the merged source at ref 7691c076, then proved end to end: the schema probe resolves 11 of 11 CANONICAL_RECEIPT_MODELS against the installed 2.3.0 wheel.

contract_model_modules_note: Modules the schema probe searches for canonical receipt models. The contracts package is walked including its submodules; GroupResolution (Cursor's ResolveReceipt) lives in group_resolver.py and is not re-exported from contracts, so it must be named explicitly. Verified against the merged source at the bound ref, not inferred.
